takeaway: Raw audio is encoded by a CNN into latent speech representations Z, which fork: spans of Z are masked and the continuous latents go through a Transformer to context representations C, while the unmasked Z is quantized into targets Q; at each masked step a contrastive loss L_m makes c_t pick out its true q_t.

reader_questions.glance: What goes in, what is masked, what is predicted, and against what?
reader_questions.detail: Where do the targets come from (quantization of the unmasked latents) and where is the loss computed (masked steps only)?

concepts.name: Fork and converge (left to right)
concepts.takes: BEST-RQ's composition: one input forks into a masked branch through the encoder and an unmasked branch through the quantizer/codebook, the two meet at the targets, and only the masked span is wired to the objective; rotated to read left to right so it fits the 5.5 in text width.
concepts.sketch: row 1: waveform X -> CNN feature encoder -> latent row Z; Z forks up (mask) to a masked row -> Transformer -> context row C (top), and down to the quantization module -> target row Q (bottom); C and Q meet at L_m between them on the right; red cells = masked steps, only they feed L_m.

concepts.name: Bottom-up tower
concepts.takes: HuBERT's tower: waveform at the base, CNN encoder, frame row with masked cells, Transformer, output row; prediction arrows only from masked columns; target branch beside the tower.
concepts.sketch: waveform / CNN / Z / masked Z / Transformer / C stacked bottom-up, quantizer and Q on the right, L_m on top.

concepts.name: Named token rows
concepts.takes: BEATs' per-position token rows with grey [M] cells, each row named in plain words on the right, network stages as wide bands between rows.
concepts.sketch: Z, masked Z, C and Q drawn as full-width token rows with names on the right; CNN, Transformer, quantizer as bands; loss banner on top.

why: wav2vec 2.0's structure IS a fork: the same latents Z go masked into the Transformer and unmasked into the quantizer, and the two branches meet only at the contrastive loss. The fork puts that in one straight-lined picture (every edge horizontal or vertical, no wrap-around), keeps a wide ~2.7:1 aspect for the 5.5 in NeurIPS text width, and shows each data state (waveform, Z, masked Z, C, Q) as data. The tower is ~1:1 at this width and needs a long detour for the target branch; full-width token rows make 4 bands plus 3 network bands, too much for a 10-second read.
highlight: The contrastive objective is the contribution's centre: one red accent (the loss colour) marks the masked time steps in C (c_t) and in Q (q_t: the true target plus the K distractors drawn from the other masked steps) and the contrastive loss L_m; only those red cells send arrows into L_m, labelled c_t and q_t + K distractors. Masked cells of the Transformer input are flat grey (the shared learned mask vector). Network boxes stay muted.
